external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A library member using the library app to borrow, renew, or reserve books.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.
external_entities.notes: The sources do not state how members authenticate to the app.

external_entities.name: desk staff
external_entities.description: Library desk staff who make manual changes to loan and member-account records.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand
external_entities.notes: The transcript states that all desk staff use one shared login and that individual staff and branches cannot be identified from the history.

processes.name: library app
processes.description: The app on a member's phone that calls the lending API for borrowing, renewal, and reservation actions.
processes.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API.

processes.name: self-service kiosk
processes.description: A branch kiosk where members scan their library card and books and which sends loan and return information to the lending API.
processes.source_excerpt: The kiosks are in every branch and they send each loan and each return to the lending API as it is scanned.

processes.name: lending API
processes.description: The REST service through which loans are accessed and changed.
processes.source_excerpt: It's a REST API. JSON in, JSON out.
processes.notes: Sources disagree about exposure. Lending service note: "The lending API is internal-only." Interview transcript: "The phones talk straight to the lending API over the internet." Authentication is also unresolved: Priya said, "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in," and could not confirm what it accepts or does with rejected calls.

processes.name: circulation page
processes.description: The circulation page served by the lending API and used by desk staff to make manual loan and account changes.
processes.source_excerpt: someone at the desk opens the circulation page and marks it returned, or clears the block on the account.
processes.notes: The text describes the circulation page as served by the lending API but does not establish it as a separately running component.

data_stores.name: loans database
data_stores.description: The database containing members, names, email addresses, home addresses, borrowing history, loans, and reservations.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Names, email addresses, home addresses and every member's full borrowing history live in the loans database.
data_stores.notes: The interview corrects the earlier statement about two databases: "We merged those in the spring. It's one loans database now. The old reservations database is gone."

data_flows.name: borrow books
data_flows.description: A member uses the library app to borrow, renew, or reserve a book.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.
data_flows.data_description: Member, book, renewal, and reservation requests.

data_flows.name: renew or reserve
data_flows.description: The library app calls the lending API to renew a loan or reserve a title.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API. It says which book and which member
data_flows.notes: Priya said, "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in," but said she could not confirm what the API accepts or does with an unacceptable call.
data_flows.data_description: The selected book or title and member information for renewal or reservation.

data_flows.name: send loans
data_flows.description: A kiosk sends scanned loan and return information to the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The kiosks are in every branch and they send each loan and each return to the lending API as it is scanned.
data_flows.data_description: Library card, book, loan, and return information.

data_flows.name: change loans
data_flows.description: Desk staff use the circulation page served by the lending API to extend loans, clear account blocks, or mark books returned.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand, through a circulation page the lending API serves.
data_flows.notes: The shared desk login means the individual staff member and branch cannot be identified.

data_flows.name: read and write loans
data_flows.description: The lending API reads and writes the loans database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The API is the only thing that reads or writes it.
data_flows.data_description: Member, loan, reservation, borrowing-history, and account records.

trust_boundaries.name: branch network
trust_boundaries.description: The network on which branch kiosks and desk staff operate.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The kiosks sit on the branch network.

trust_boundaries.name: council data centre
trust_boundaries.description: The council data-centre zone where the lending API and loans database run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The lending API and the loans database run in the council data centre.

assumptions.assumption: The loans database is confidential because it contains names, email addresses, home addresses, and members' full borrowing histories.
assumptions.basis: The interview states that these personal and borrowing-history records live in the loans database.

assumptions.assumption: The council data centre is a network trust boundary.
assumptions.basis: The lending API and loans database are explicitly stated to run in the council data centre, which is modeled as a distinct location-based zone.

assumptions.assumption: The branch network is a network trust boundary.
assumptions.basis: The kiosks and desk staff are explicitly placed on the branch network, which is modeled as a distinct network location.

assumptions.assumption: The lending API presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: The source describes it as a REST API; REST is classified as a web application interface by the extraction rules.
